questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The nature and the fact that it was an english speaking country. They also had guaranteed student accommodation.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was the best experience in my life and I can definetely recommend everyone to go on exchange!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, I got a lot of emails from the University about everything I needed to know.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I stayed at Uniflats and when I arrived to pick up the key for my house they offered to drive me to my accommodation and help me with all that I needed. There was also a orientation week with a lot of orientation events and a campus tour where they told us all the practical stuff that we had to do.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Overall, it was good, but there was not that many social events in the orientation week. However, I still found friends very easily so it didn't matter that much.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I stayed at UniFlats and it was very easy to find it. You got an email with how to sign up and then you just fill in a survey about yourself and then they try to match you with people that fit with your personality. Usually you stay with other exchange students and one local kiwi.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It was only five minutes away from campus so it felt like almost staying at campus. Almost all the students lived in the same area very close to campus, which was very nice. I can really recommend UniFlats.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UniFlats was amazing and it was a very easy way to get to know people. I became very good friends with my flatmates and we ended up doing a lot of things together, including movie nights, going to Mt cook and flat dinners. The houses are not very well isolated so they are a little bit cold in winter, but that was the only bad thing about it.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a while ago that i did it, but I remember it as being pretty straight forward.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: On your student account there is a section for the course registration. You have to fill in a form for each course you want to take if it has any prerequisites, where I just uploaded my transscript from UCPH. You could also change courses after arrival if you changed your mind about which courses you wanted to take. They have no limit on how many students that can take a course, so you can basically choose whatever you want as long as you live up to the criteria.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could go to AskOtago at the university library or write emails to them and they where very helpful. If you wrote them an email they would usually answer within a day.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was very easy and I got all the classes that I wanted since they have no limit on how many students that can sign up for each course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get your "forhåndsgodkendelse" from UCPH as fast as possible so you know which courses you can apply for. And if you are in doubt of which courses to take, you can always change it once you get there, so dont worry so much.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The courses were nice but the academic level was a bit lower than in Denmark. They didnt have that many courses to choose from compared to Denmark but overall I ended up finding som interesting courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took a 100-level paper (introductory) and two 300-level papers (3rd year papers). Papers are the same as courses. The level was not too hard but you had to do a lot of assignments and work during the course that also counted in your final grade.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In general it varied from course to course but it was pretty similar. You had more assignments. There was almost no oral presentations but that varies from course to course. It depended a lot on which courses you took but in general the style of teaching were lectures and tutorials or lab work.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
GEOL 112: Dynamic Earth: A New Zealand Perspective
GEOG 393: Plants, People and the Environment
ENVI 312: Intedisciplinary Aspects of Climate Change

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
GEOl112 had 3 field trips in the local area which was really nice if you like doing field work. 
ENVI312 gave a broad introduction to climate change from a lot of different perspectives which I really liked. I also liked GEOG393 but that is mostly relevant if you study geography or ecology.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: We spent a lot of money on car rentals and gas since none of my friends had a car.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping were more expensive than in Denmark but it was based on seasons. In the winter a cucumber would cost 5$ (20dkk) and a bell pepper would be the same. But eating out was cheaper than in Denmark. A coffee would be roughly 4.8-5$ (so 20dkk ish).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of clubs and sports that you could join. They had a skiing club, tramping club (hiking), surfing etc. One of my friends also did rowing. They had a place called OUSA that offered a lot of activities including a sauna. I mostly used the free gym where I joined a lot of their group fitness classes which I can really recommend.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The people from UniFlats arranged a lot of social activities like parties, barbeques and quiznights which was mostly for other exchange students. You could also go to the museum for free. Other than that there was a free gym and lots of clubs and societies. The tramping club was probably the most popular one which would take you on hiking trips.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The free gym and the group fitness, because it is an easy way to get some exercise and you can go whenever you want. 
The activities arranged by Uniflats because it was a good way to meet and socialize with other exchange students.
The tramping club: I did not join it but I have heard from other people that it is a lot of fun and a great way to also meet some locals.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Going on trips! Roy's Peak (it is in Wanaka), Queenstown (both skiing and bungyjumping), the Catlins, Mt Cook, Abel Tasman (it is a bit far away but you can go in the mid-semester break). Do a trip to the North Island if you have a longer holiday or have time after the study has finished. Go and watch a Rugby Match, Otago Museum (it is free)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. It is basically the same culture as Denmark but more relaxed.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs or talk with them in class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There was not really any cultural differences.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really liked the Maori culture which was very different from Denmark, and they are more connected with nature. I liked that the culture in the country in general was very relaxed and laid back. For example you adressed the teachers by their first name and everyone was wearing shorts and relaxed clothes.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Take time to explore the beautiful nature in the country!
Explore some of the Maori culture by fx going to a marae or a maori event.
Rent or buy a car. It is impossible to go anywhere without a car.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everyone is very helpful and friendly. Dunedin has a perfect location for going on trips around the South Island so take advantage of that!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I made and all the trips that we went on together.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
That the exams were hand written.
Jetlag.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
New Zealand is a beautiful country if you love nature, mountains, hiking and adventure.
They also have a lot of wildlife like albatros, penguins and sea lions (and of course the kiwi).
Go to New Zealand on exchange if you also like that.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
